text: A parameter is defined at the pipeline level, and genuinely can't be modified during a run at all. It controls the pipeline's behavior from outside — connection details, a file path, which environment to target — supplied the moment the pipeline starts, either as a default value or an explicit one passed in directly.

A variable, by contrast, can actually be set and modified while the pipeline is running, using the Set Variable activity. It's for storing and tracking real state as the pipeline progresses — the result of a computation, a flag an If Condition checks later, a running list an Append Variable activity builds up over time.

The whole distinction really comes down to one sentence. Parameters are external, set once, from outside a pipeline. Variables are internal, mutable, changed from inside a pipeline as it actually runs. If a value needs to come in from whoever starts the pipeline, that's a parameter. If a value needs to change while the pipeline is running, that's a variable.

One real gotcha worth remembering: variables are scoped to the entire pipeline, not to any one activity or loop, which means they're genuinely not thread-safe. Setting a variable inside a ForEach activity running in parallel can produce unpredictable results, since every parallel iteration races to read and write that exact same variable at once. If you need a genuinely per-iteration value inside a parallel loop, pass it as a parameter to an Execute Pipeline activity instead, which Lesson 21 covers in full — each invocation gets its own independent scope, with nothing shared to race against. Next: If Condition and Switch — branching a pipeline's actual path based on exactly these kinds of values.
